the_act.title: Calendar (New Style) Act 1750 (24 Geo. 2 c. 23)
the_act.publisher: The National Archives / legislation.gov.uk, the United Kingdom's official statute service
the_act.status: primary source, read in full at the address above and quoted from it
quoted_on_the_page: the natural day next immediately following the said second day of September shall be called, reckoned, and accounted to be the fourteenth day of September, omitting for that time only the eleven intermediate nominal days of the common calendar
hath been received and established, and is now generally practised by almost all other nations of Europe
the_act.why_it_is_load_bearing: The first quotation is the only evidence this work needs for its central claim, and it is a primary one: the statute omits NOMINAL days and says so in that word, while the natural day next immediately following is expressly carried over. The second establishes, from the same document, that the eleven numbers it omitted were in ordinary use elsewhere in Europe on those days.

the_census_itself.what_it_is: This practice's own measurement, made on 2026-09-20 on the machine this session ran on. It is not a source; it is the evidence.
the_census_itself.how_to_reproduce: Run each script in census/ with an output directory, then build.py with the same directory. The sixteen answer files are 160 332 lines each and are not committed; the SHA-256 of every one of them is in counts.json, so a later run can be compared with this one byte for byte.
the_census_itself.the_machine: Python 3.11.15, SQLite 3.45.1, Ruby 3.3.6, Java 21.0.10 (OpenJDK), Node 22.22.2, PHP 8.4.19, Perl 5.38.2, GNU coreutils 9.4, glibc via gcc 13.3.0, Go 1.24.7 was present but its answers duplicate the C library's and it was left out of the bench.

not_verified_against_an_original.claim: That the papal bull Inter gravissimas of 1582 struck ten days, 5 to 14 October, from the calendar of the states that adopted it.
not_verified_against_an_original.note: Widely reported and not in dispute. This work did not read the bull. Nothing measured on the page depends on it: what is measured is that two of the sixteen readers refuse exactly those ten written dates, which is a fact about the readers.

not_verified_against_an_original.claim: That Sweden kept a 30 February in 1712.
not_verified_against_an_original.note: Reported in the calendrical literature, with a photograph of a 1712 Swedish almanac page published online. This practice did not see an original or an archival scan tonight and does not assert it as fact. What is measured is that nine readers refuse the written date and the seven that take it hand back a day already named.

not_verified_against_an_original.claim: That Russia's change of calendar in 1918 struck thirteen days, 1 to 13 February.
not_verified_against_an_original.note: Reported in secondary sources; the text of the decree was not located tonight. What is measured is that no reader of the sixteen refuses any of those written dates.
